version.changelog: 0.2.0: refined triggering description (hand-reviewed, not benchmarked — the automated trigger-scoring harness could not detect skill triggering via 'claude -p' in this environment). Sharpens the trigger to a self-running loop with a judged outcome + real stop condition, and explicitly excludes near-misses: literal loop code, plain vercel.json/GitHub-Actions cron, and the Vercel Workflow product. Skill body unchanged.

llm.summary: The skill mostly gives coherent guidance for building supervised recurring agent loops, but it also tells agents to ignore certain mandatory session or hook instructions, which is a real control-bypass concern.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks agents to create scheduled cloud routines, local hooks, worktrees, command allowlists, and state files. These are proportionate to recurring automation when user-directed, but users should scope them carefully because they can affect repositories and cost.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a single Markdown skill file and no executable scripts or install-time code were present in the inspected workspace.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact explicitly says to ignore some 'MANDATORY: run Skill(X)' session or prompt-hook instructions and that the user's request takes precedence unless the agent deems the skill genuinely relevant. That attempts to override external routing or safety controls and is not necessary for loop-building.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent behavior is disclosed: loop state is written to disk, scheduled routines may commit and push state, and hooks may run locally. The skill includes mitigations such as hard stops, proof runs, autonomy levels, deny rules, and human approval before push/merge.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to build self-running agent loops with triggers, state files, hard gates, allowlists, and supervised rollout; creating routines, hooks, and persistent state is high-impact but broadly aligned with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Its loop-building guidance is practical and mostly safety-conscious, but the instruction to ignore certain mandatory skill-routing hooks should be removed or replaced with hierarchy-preserving guidance. Use only with narrowly scoped commands, objective stop conditions, manual proof runs, and explicit approval for any scheduled routine, hook, commit, push, merge, or publish action.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The autonomous-loop behavior is the skill's core purpose and is disclosed with several guardrails, including objective gates, max-iteration backstops, proof runs, cost estimates, and starting at low autonomy.
[AE1] unexpected: I inspected the full required SKILL.md locally; the referenced artifact was available and complete, so this finding does not support escalation.
[TM1] unexpected: The cited 'git push --force' text appears in an explicit deny list of dangerous commands, not as an instruction to run it.
[RA2] expected: Inlining procedures and persisting state are expected for scheduled cloud routines, and the skill discloses why; this remains a risk to manage but is not hidden or unrelated.
[SSD-1] unexpected: This concern is supported by the artifact: the skill tells agents to ignore some mandatory hook-injected skill instructions based on its own relevance judgment, which can bypass host instruction routing.
[AS3] unexpected: The cited path is a worked example of a newly created procedure file, not an instruction to enumerate or read unrelated installed skills.
[T01] unexpected: The static finding is supported by lines 160-165: the skill attempts to set precedence over session or prompt-hook skill routing, which is a purpose-mismatched instruction-scope issue.
